text: TOKENS ARE VERY LIMITED: short replies; the person wants "focused and spartan" answers (ADHD-friendly: only the answer); no long essays; workers read only what they need.

UI RULE 0 (top priority): numbers and actions align in fixed grid columns (right-aligned tabular numbers, actions in one fixed column, titles ellipsize) so it is readable at a glance. Also: do not limit UI width (full size). See docs/UI-CHECKLIST.md (derived from the installed ui-ux-pro-max skill, ~/.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max: use only its UX guidelines search, `python3 ~/.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py "<topic>" --domain ux -n 3` WITHOUT -I).

Workers: Haiku 5.5 subagents do the work; the head (Sonnet/Opus) plans and verifies. Opus 5.5 (medium/low effort) is allowed whenever advice/design/review is needed ("feel free"), kept short. Cursor Auto (tools/cursor-review2.sh, needs the person's VPN ON) for independent security/code reviews (read-only, uses Cursor quota). agy staff (Gemini 3.8 Flash, UNLIMITED quota, weak model; needs VPN + a Google login: if 403 'log out and log back in' the person must run `agy` and /login) for small atomic read-only audits, gap lists, fixtures, drafts from a facts file; read docs/AGY-PLAYBOOK.md; ALWAYS verify agy output with a Haiku (about 30-40% of its facts are wrong in doc edits). Never ask agy to run code, do security logic, UI visuals, or multi-file refactors. Run via tools/agy-queue.py (AGY_MAX env, default 3).

Parallelism: only file overlap limits it; give every worker a strict file list; workers stage ONLY their own files by explicit path (never `git add -A`, never reset the index); shared files (routes.js, app.js, state.js, cli.py, cmdops.py) need minimal re-read-before-edit hunks.

The person wants the head NOT to be idle while tasks exist ("this is the rule: dont be idle as head") BUT the LATEST instructions override: "after running tasks done, don't start new tasks at all" and "stop the tasks": everything is stopped now. Only start work when asked.

Always register jobs on the dashboard (hooks do it when the Agent description contains a real task id), close with tokens, update tasks.json notes, sync the board, commit, push. Show the roadmap/state at the end of every job.

Worker prompts must always say: never `usage sync`, never read the keychain, no network, NEVER execute `roadmap service|serve|hooks install|usage sync` (parse only), TEMP ROADMAP_HOME for runs, never touch the launchd service / real ~/.config/roadmap-board / split_net / ~/.claude, never touch port 8780 or the person's browser tabs (use own port + own new tab with explicit tabId), spawn no subagents, do not push (the head pushes). One worker once broke this and ran service install/restart: the service was verified healthy.
Browser: never drive the person's dashboard tab; open new tabs and close them.
Fresh session at ~70% context; keep the checkpoint current. When weekly usage nears the stop, report instead of continuing.

split-net project rules (memory, in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-ali-Works-split-net/memory/): never risk the person's VPN (Claude session depends on it: no flaps, no global TUN on the live machine), macOS only, use own core VPN for VPN tests, agent-first CLI, etc. They matter only if you touch split-net.

Be the head like before: parallel workers on disjoint files, verify, register, commit, push; never idle; Opus (medium/high) for design advice and think-heavy features; agy (unlimited, verified) and Cursor (auto or grok-4.7-xhigh, NOT API) as much as possible; Haiku edits.

Issues must be part of Work/board (not a separate section); Work must be interactive (+ Add anything: task, issue, idea->Backlog, question, subtask, comment); a Backlog status/column; Work like Trello (docs/WORK-V2-SPEC.md).
Tokens section must be SIMPLE: usage now + limit per PROJECT (one number) + one weekly stop; no tiny settings.
Rules section must show both projects' rules (done: 12 each). Planner = project structure plan tree (done). Workflow map = FigJam-like flow start->now (done) + open in new tab (R7.30).

A Git section (history, branches, auto commit/push policy, agents work close to git) (docs/GIT-SPEC.md). A Head section (R7.31, top priority). A full UI+core log for debugging what the person tests (R7.16).
Always care for UI/UX with the ui-ux-pro-max skill after every wave and file tasks from it (UX routine in HEAD-RUNBOOK).
The side panel must be reopenable (done: top-bar toggle). Drag on the map must not select text (done).

The **request ledger**: every person message that contains an ask, decision, rule, bug report or preference is logged (who said it, when, verbatim text, a short auto-summary, a kind: ask | decision | rule | bug | preference | question) with full detail on demand.

How the head (the AI session) **captures** them reliably and cheaply: a CLI (`roadmap head log "<verbatim>" --kind ... --task ...`), hooks (UserPromptSubmit hook can append every person message to the ledger automatically: investigate what the Claude Code hook payload gives), the docs/HANDOVER + memory sync, and the `/head` skill reading the ledger on resume so a new chat needs NO re-explaining.

**Conversion and traceability**: each ledger entry links to what it became (issue / task / review / backlog item / rule / feature / decision), with a lifecycle status: new -> understood -> bound -> in progress -> done | declined | needs-you; "did the head act on it?" = a visible flag and age ('unhandled for 2 h'); coverage view (uncovered asks), done/accepted by the person only.

The **GUI section** "Head": who is head now (model, session start, usage), a timeline/list of asks with summary + status chips + the bound tasks, expand for the verbatim text, filters (unhandled, in progress, done), a one-line Overview chip ('3 asks unhandled'), copy-ref support, phone read-only; aligned grid (UI rule 0), CSS budget (cap 72 KB).
Smartness: auto-summarise, auto-suggest the conversion (ask -> task vs issue vs review) and duplicates/merge, detect unfulfilled asks from old sessions, keep per-account-switch continuity.
Safety/privacy (no secrets), data model compatible with the existing files, Haiku-sized build breakdown with strict file lists, Cursor grok review gate, agy audits.
